newsitem.title: USA: Clinton aims to revive community riverfronts.
newsitem.headline: Clinton aims to revive community riverfronts.

text.p: President Clinton's plan to establish "American Heritage rivers" will help protect, restore and revive riverfronts that used to be the hearts of communities across the nation, a White House official said Wednesday.
In his State of the Union Address Tuesday Clinton said he will designate "10 American Heritage rivers to help communities alongside them revitalise their waterfronts and clean up pollution."

A White House official said Clinton will designate 10 stretches of rivers the first year and that he will be looking for rivers central to the history and development of a community, and rivers communities are willing to spend their own resources to improve.
"Just about everywhere there's a river there's a town that's trying to bring it back and make it a more vital part of their town again," the official said.

"We saw a great opportunity to bring the environmental agencies and the agencies that deal with the humanities and historic preservation and recreation to work better with towns that are trying to do this," he said.

The official said the administration will pull together recommendations for the programme over the next 90 days, getting suggestions from around the country. They will then take nominations from communities for the designation.
The programme was not supposed to cost more federal dollars, but might mean reallocating resources, the official said.

He said the administration will assign someone to work almost as a "caseworker" for the heritage river area, who will help put together a plan and guide communities through the maze of various federal programmes that could help them.
"We have parks and scenic rivers, but there isn't really anything for rivers where people live and certainly nothing that brings all our federal programmes together," he said.
